dataset_metadata.name: Experimental degradation study of a commercial lithium-ion battery (TUM bawaii)
dataset_metadata.citation: Wildfeuer, L.; Karger, A.; Aygül, D.; Wassiliadis, N.; Jossen, A.; Lienkamp, M. (2023): Experimental degradation study of a commercial lithium-ion battery. Journal of Power Sources 560, p. 232498. DOI: 10.1016/j.jpowsour.2022.232498.
dataset_metadata.funding: Bavarian Ministry of Economic Affairs, Regional Development and Energy, Germany (project bawaii — battery analytics with artificial intelligence, IUK-1808-0013)

cell_info.cell_notes: Silicon-doped graphite anode (1.4 wt% Si). NCA formulation LiNi0.80Co0.15Al0.05O2. CCCV capacity 2.53 Ah. 10s DC resistance 32.42 mΩ at 100% SOC (experimentally determined). All 196 cells from the same production batch.

aging_modes.notes: 13 groups (A–M). Calendar aging (Groups B–G): full-factorial design in T–SOC space with three CU interval sub-groups (6, 12, 96 weeks). Cycle aging (Group H): D-optimal design with 38 test points and 72 cells across 5 stress factors (T, mean SOC, DOD, C_charge, C_discharge). Groups I–J: alternating and random stress factor cycling. Groups K–M: mixed calendar/cycling or dynamic protocol cycling. Group A: CU-only reference cell. Group X (added in dataset update): BOL-only cells. Group Y (added in dataset update): cycling followed by calendar aging. Some cells at 60°C/100% SOC reached 0 V before end of study at 697 days. Raw timeseries data is publicly available in the repository.

time_protocol.test_equipment: BaSyTec CTS; BaSyTec XCTS MKII (for high-current cycling)
time_protocol.notes: Calendar aging ran for 697 days (~23 months). Cycle aging reached up to 1500 EFC. Rest between half-cycles during cycling: t_pause = 600 s × DOD, maximum 10 min. Check-up interval for cycling: 50 EFC. Check-up intervals for calendar aging: 6 weeks (Group B), 12 weeks (Group C), 96 weeks (Group D). Group D cells received only initial and final CU (at 96 weeks / 672 days).

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Dataset updated (doi:10.14459/2024mp1734374) to include previously undescribed cells (Groups X and Y). Corrected cell overview file: bawaii_cell_overview_publication_corrected.xlsx. Newly described cells marked in yellow; researchers advised to verify test conditions for those cells.
rawdata.known_issues: Half-cell fitting algorithm fails for some cells at high storage SOCs (80–95%) after a few check-ups due to an additional peak appearing in the C/10 differential voltage. Some cells stored at 60°C/100% SOC reached 0 V at ~500 days.

checkup.notes: Check-up (CU) performed consistently at 20°C. Protocol: 3 h rest, CC discharge at 1C (I=2.5 A) to 2.5 V, 2 h rest, CCCV charge (I=0.25C, U_max=4.2V, I_cut=0.02C, t_cut=1h), CCCV discharge for capacity, slow C/10 charge for pOCV/DVA half-cell fitting (LLI, LAM_NE, LAM_PE), then 18s DC pulse at 100%, 50% and 20% SOC for resistance. SOH parameters reported: SOH_C (capacity), SOH_R (resistance), SOH_LI (LLI), SOH_NE (LAM anode), SOH_PE (LAM cathode). Calendar CU intervals: 6 weeks (Group B, ~4000+ total CUs), 12 weeks (Group C), 96 weeks (Group D). Over 4000 CU measurements in total.

notes: Dataset known as 'bawaii' (battery analytics with artificial intelligence). Original data DOI: 10.14459/2023mp1713382. Updated dataset DOI: 10.14459/2024mp1734374 (includes Groups X and Y). The D-optimal cycle aging design covered mean SOC levels 10–90% and DOD 5–100% (Table 4 stress factor levels: T in [5,20,35,50]°C, mean SOC in [10,20,30,40,50,60,80,90]%, DOD in [5,20,40,60,80,100]%, C_charge in [0.5,1,1.5,2]C, C_discharge in [1,2,5,10,14]C). The study quantifies five state-of-health parameters: capacity fade, resistance increase, LLI, LAM at negative electrode, and LAM at positive electrode. Dominant degradation mode for calendar aging is LLI; for cycling, LLI and LAM_NE. Silicon-graphite anode shows faster degradation at low SOC and at high charging currents at low temperature (lithium plating suspected).
